CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Lawrence is a 62-year-old male with past medical history significant for type 1 diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux who presents with complaints of shortness of breath for approximately 10 days. Patient reports noticing some swelling and attributes it to recent consumption of salty foods at house parties. He describes feeling lethargic. Dyspnea is exertional, occurring with stair climbing. Patient reports mild leg swelling. He notes some discomfort lying flat in bed and stiffness upon waking in the morning. He had one episode of acute nocturnal dyspnea approximately one week ago but has not experienced recurrence. Patient denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain. Regarding his diabetes, patient reports good blood sugar control during the work week but admits to inconsistent monitoring on weekends. He denies recent spikes in blood glucose. Patient acknowledges continued consumption of chocolate bars. Regarding depression, patient reports it has been a difficult year and a half. He has tried outdoor stretching exercises during summer months but notes difficulty maintaining this with weather changes. He is not ready to initiate medications at this time but is open to suggestions. For reflux, patient reports adherence to lifestyle modifications including reducing Red Bull and caffeine intake. Alcohol intake has been difficult during the holiday season but improving. Patient denies suicidal or homicidal ideation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for shortness of breath and lower extremity swelling. Negative for chest pain, fever, chills, cough, and abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 1 diabetes mellitus
Congestive heart failure
Depression
Gastroesophageal reflux disease

MEDICATIONS
Insulin pump
Omeprazole 20 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works during the week. Enjoys chocolate bars. Recent attendance at house parties with consumption of salty foods. Reducing alcohol intake, particularly noting difficulty during holiday season. Previously engaged in outdoor stretching exercises for mental health.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Within normal limits. Pulse oximetry good.
Neck: No jugular venous distension. No carotid bruits.
Heart: 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated.
Lungs: Bilateral crackles at bases.
Lower extremities: 1+ pitting edema.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease or pneumonia.
Laboratory studies: Normal white blood cell count. No evidence of infection.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute heart failure exacerbation: Start lasix 40 mg daily. Patient instructed to weigh self daily and report if weight is not decreasing or if increasing. Patient to call or go to emergency room if dyspnea worsens at rest or with minimal activity. May require intravenous diuretics if symptoms progress.

2. Type 1 diabetes mellitus: Order hemoglobin A1c in approximately one month to assess need for medication adjustments. Patient to follow up with endocrinologist. Ensure recent eye exam has been completed.

3. Depression: Refer to psychiatry for talk therapy. No medications initiated at this time.

4. Gastroesophageal reflux disease: Continue omeprazole 20 mg daily.

Patient instructed to contact provider if any problems with breathing develop.
